title: Statement on glibc/iconv Vulnerability
content:
EDIT 2024-04-25: Clarified when a PHP application is vulnerable to this bug.

Recently, a bug in version 2.39 and older () was uncovered where a buffer overflow in character set conversions the ISO-2022-CN-EXT character set can result in remote code execution. glibctoCVE-2024-2961

This specific buffer overflow in glibc is exploitable through PHP, which exposes the iconv functionality of glibc to do character set conversions via the . Although the bug is exploitable in the context of the PHP Engine, the bug is not in PHP. It is also not directly exploitable remotely. iconv extension

The bug is exploitable, , the PHP application calls iconv or with user-supplied character sets. if and only iffunctionsfilters

Applications are vulnerable if: not

Moreover, when using a user-supplied character set, it is good practice for applications to accept only specific charsets that have been explicitly allowed by the application. One example of how this can be done is by using an allow-list and the function to check the encoding before passing it to iconv. For example: array_search()array_search($charset, $allowed_list, true)

There are numerous reports online with titles like "Mitigating the iconv Vulnerability for PHP (CVE-2024-2961)" or "PHP Under Attack". These titles are misleading as this is a bug in PHP itself.not

If your PHP application is vulnerable, we first recommend to check if your Linux distribution has already published patched variants of glibc. , CentOS, and others, have already done so, and please upgrade as soon as possible. Debian

Once an update is available in glibc, updating that package on your Linux machine will be enough to alleviate the issue. You do not need to update PHP, as glibc is a dynamically linked library.

If your Linux distribution has not published a patched version of glibc, there is no fix for this issue. However, there exists a workaround described in which explains a way on how to remove the problematic character set from glibc. Perform this procedure for every gconv-modules-extra.conf file that is available on your system.GLIBC Vulnerability on Servers Serving PHP

PHP users on Windows are not affected.

Therefore, a new version of PHP will not be released for this vulnerability.

  • Glibc security updates from the distribution have been installed.
  • Or the iconv extension is not loaded.
  • Or the vulnerable character set has been removed from gconv-modules-extra.conf.
  • Or the application passes only specifically allowed character sets to iconv.
